steps.tx: Epithelial ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynaecological malignancy, commonly diagnosed at stage III or IV due to insidious peritoneal dissemination. **High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma** characteristically arises from the fimbriated end of the fallopian tube via serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma STIC lesions with ubiquitous TP53 mutations. Precursor secretory cells detach from fimbriae and implant upon ovarian and pelvic peritoneal surfaces.

steps.tx: The scans show a complex pelvic mass with cake like omental thickening, scattered peritoneal implants, and fluid filling the abdomen. This pattern defines advanced **high grade serous carcinoma**, which spreads silently from tubal **STIC** precursors carrying **TP53** mutation. Recognizing diffuse peritoneal disease explains why most patients present at stage three or four.
steps.say: This is the classic face of advanced high grade serous ovarian cancer. A complex adnexal mass seeds the peritoneum, building omental cake, multiple implants, and malignant ascites across the abdomen. The lesson traces this spread to precursor cells leaving the tubal fimbriae after TP53 change. For exams, link a pelvic mass plus omental cake plus ascites with advanced serous carcinoma and late stage diagnosis.

vis.alt: Abdominal CT shows a pelvic mass with omental cake, peritoneal implants, and malignant ascites.
vis.caption: CT shows advanced ovarian cancer with peritoneal spread. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Maximal surgical cytoreduction serves as the cornerstone of upfront management. Primary **cytoreductive surgery** aims for complete macroscopic resection R0, which provides the most critical independent determinant of progression-free and overall survival. Surgical debulking encompasses total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, total omentectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy, and peritonectomy or bowel resections necessary to remove all visible deposits.

left.title: Complete Cytoreduction (R0)
points: Goal of all primary debulking attempts

right.title: Suboptimal Cytoreduction
points: Higher rate of early platinum resistance

steps.tx: Standard frontline systemic chemotherapy combines platinum and taxane doublets. First-line systemic therapy for advanced ovarian cancer is **carboplatin AUC** 5 to 6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 every 3 weeks for 6 cycles, with or without bevacizumab in GOG-0218. In GOG-0218, adding concurrent and maintenance bevacizumab extended progression-free survival, particularly in suboptimally debulked stage IV disease.

rows: GOG-0218 (PFS benefit in stage IV / sub-optimal)

steps.tx: Targeted maintenance therapy exploits homologous recombination deficiency. **Maintenance olaparib** for 2 years significantly prolongs progression-free survival in newly diagnosed advanced BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer, reducing progression risk by 70% in SOLO-1. Long-term seven-year follow-up demonstrated a median PFS of 56.0 months with olaparib compared to 13.8 months with placebo, solidifying PARP inhibition as upfront standard of care.

nodes.label: Olaparib maintenance 300 mg bid x 2 years (SOLO-1)

steps.tx: PARP maintenance indications have expanded across broader biomarker groups. Maintenance **niraparib** provides significant progression-free survival benefit across all advanced ovarian cancer patients responding to platinum, regardless of BRCA mutation or HRD status in PRIMA. Niraparib is dosed using individualized baseline platelet count and body weight to minimize grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia, offering substantial benefit in homologous recombination-deficient tumours.

right.title: PRIMA (Overall Population / HR-Proficient)
points: Statistically significant benefit regardless of HRD

steps.tx: Therapeutic decision-making in recurrent disease depends on treatment-free interval. **Platinum-sensitive** recurrence occurring 6 months or more after completing frontline platinum is retreated with platinum doublets and maintenance PARP inhibitors. Doublet regimens include carboplatin plus gemcitabine, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or paclitaxel. Conversely, platinum-resistant disease recurring within 6 months mandates non-platinum monotherapy.

steps.tx: Folate receptor alpha targeted therapy overcomes cytotoxic resistance in recurrent disease. **Mirvetuximab soravtansine** is an antibody-drug conjugate targeting folate receptor alpha FRalpha, improving overall survival in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in the MIRASOL trial. Mirvetuximab delivers the potent microtubule-disrupting maytansinoid DM4 to tumour cells demonstrating high FRalpha positivity on immunohistochemistry.

steps.tx: Direct intraperitoneal delivery achieves high regional drug concentration with minimal systemic toxicity. Hyperthermic **intraperitoneal chemotherapy** HIPEC with cisplatin at interval cytoreductive surgery improves progression-free and overall survival in stage 3 ovarian cancer. Performed after three neoadjuvant chemotherapy cycles, cisplatin 100 mg/m2 circulated at 40 to 41 degrees Celsius for 90 minutes added significant survival benefit in the Dutch OVHIPEC-1 trial.

left.title: OVHIPEC-1 Protocol
points: Stage III disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 at 40-41 deg C for 90 min
Median OS improved from 33.9 to 45.7 months

right.title: Intravenous Chemotherapy Alone
points: Post-operative cycles 4 to 6 of IV chemo
Higher rate of peritoneal cavity recurrence
